Jahresabrechnung 2025: Heizkosten 1.000 €, Warmwasser 200 €. No Zählerstände, which is the normal case: the NK window says 'No Zählerstände for this flat'. out/s5-main.out: Eva 'Heizkosten 293.15 (by days) · Warmwasser 58.63 (by days)'.

out/s5-head.out: Eva 'Heizkosten 787.95 (Grundkosten 30 % by days · consumption by days lived 107 of 107) · Warmwasser 157.59'. Her letter says 'Heizkosten (Grundkosten 30 % nach Tagen · Verbrauch nach bewohnten Tagen 107 von 107) 787,95 €'. The Leerstand row (01.01.–15.09., 258 days) shows 'consumption 0'.

So a tenant who lived there 29 % of the year is billed 79 % of the year's Heizkosten and Warmwasser, including the empty winter months: about 594 € more than by time.

In k1r-heat H1 (15 empty days) the Leerstand drops from 93,21 € (main) to 58,68 € (head), with 'cons 0'.

Cause: _srConsSplit, when how === 'days' (no meters), gives the whole 70 % V only to the stays (v = V × days / occ, leerV = 0). The NK window says 'only among the stays · never the Leerstand'.

Without a Zwischenablesung, HeizkostenV § 9b (3) requires the whole cost to be split by Gradtagzahlen or by time between the users, and the empty days are the owner's. That conflicts with R5's 'never more than the real cost; empty days stay with the owner by law'. findings.fix: In _srConsSplit, when there are no usable meter readings (how === 'days'), split the 70 % part by time over the whole period, so the Leerstand keeps V × empty days / perDays (leerV), the way the 30 % part is split. Or split it by Gradtagzahlen. Keep 'consumption only among the stays' for the meter case, where the empty days get their measured share. The letter text 'Verbrauch nach bewohnten Tagen 107 von 107' then follows that split.
